# scope-fe BOM, one board (generated by `kicad/gen/gen_bom.py`; do not edit by hand)

From the root netlist `kicad/export/scope-fe.net` (450 fitted parts, 108 lines). Prices in USD for one board: LCSC ladder price at the board quantity (or the LCSC minimum order), verified on 24 Nov 2026; a non-LCSC offer (`docs/research/prices.md`) is used where it is lower. `no stock` = listed but fewer in stock than needed. Full table: `docs/bom.csv`.

Not included: PCB (6-layer JLC06161H-3313, impedance control), assembly, shipping, USB-C supply.

## JLCPCB part classes

Column `JLC class`: `basic` = JLCPCB basic library (no per-part set-up fee), `extended` = JLCPCB extended library (set-up fee per unique extended part and order, about 3 USD each at the time of writing), `not JLC` = PCB feature or footprint-only. Source: the jlcpcb.com parts API listing of the basic library (componentLibraryType `base`, 351 parts on 24 Nov 2026; it agrees with the per-part flags in `kicad/gen/lcsc_parts.py`). Status `ok` = LCSC or JLC stock covers the board quantity (JLC assembles from its own stock; some basic parts show 0 at LCSC but millions at JLC).

| | lines | unique parts | parts placed |
|---|---|---|---|
| basic | 53 | 53 | 337 |
| extended | 28 | 27 | 113 |
| fitted part lines / unique LCSC parts | 81 | 80 | 450 |

BOM optimisation of 24 Nov 2026 (SPEC decisions 25 and 26): 103 -> 94 fitted part lines, 74 -> 58 extended part numbers, 20 -> 2 resistors at 0.1 %, 73.13 -> 70.45 USD. **BOM review 2 (24 Nov 2026, SPEC decisions 27-34**, user review of the extended-part list; studies `docs/research/bom2-trigger.md`, `bom2-input-taps.md`, `bom2-power-passives.md`): TMUX136 -> two BAT15-04W diode bridges, SN65LVDS2 -> 9th COS3502, RV101 trimmer removed (firmware LF/HF correction), C101 50 V +/-0.05 pF, tap coupling caps 0.5 pF +/-0.05 pF (Murata), +5V1 divider 1 % (no 0.1 % part left), inductors 4 -> 3 types, beads 3 -> 2 types, PTC -> 0 R, TVS DNP, tantalum -> 4 x (1 R + 47 uF) MLCC damper, TLV9001 -> TPH2501, BAT15-03W -> half a BAT15-04W, resistor and sub-1 nF capacitor values moved to JLC basic parts: 94 -> 81 fitted part lines, 58 -> 27 extended part numbers, 0 resistors at 0.1 %, 70.45 -> 70.39 USD. Remaining extended passives: 1.5 / 2.2 / 3.3 / 0.5 pF (no basic C0G below 10 pF), 1 nF C0G servo Cint (no basic C0G above 100 pF), the 0402 GHz beads BLM15HD102SN1D, the inductors (no basic power inductor) and the DLW21SN900HQ2L balun.

## LCSC verification

Checked per part: MPN, value, tolerance, dielectric / voltage rating, package against the board footprint, LCSC stock (column Stock) and the price at the ladder step nearest 10 pcs (column P~10).

## If the budget gets tight: cheapest cuts

The board is under budget; these are the options in order of cost per USD saved, should prices move:

1. **SMA connectors** (2 x 4.68, Samtec SMA-J-P-H-ST-EM1 C5199907): generic LCSC edge-launch SMAs are 0.5-2.0 (the RF Solutions CON-SMA-EDGE-S C5356059 was out of stock on 24 Nov 2026); saves up to ~8, but needs a footprint check (1.6 mm board fit, >3 GHz rating).
2. **GVA-84+ -> TRF37D73** in the phase-strobe chains: saves ~3, but sim/strobe/RESULT.md gives only 2.15 V per line (below the 2.75 V the taps need with the 80 ps stub). Not recommended.
3. **TLV3801 -> TLV3601** (single-ended output): saves ~0.5, needs a redesign of the LVDS split. Not worth it.
4. (Done, BOM review 2) RV101 trimmer removed, no 0.1 % resistors, TMUX136 / SN65LVDS2 / TLV9001 replaced.
